summary: Agent implemented the checkbox directly (3 tool calls: ls, git status, Read, then Edit) with no brainstorming skill invocation. index.html now contains <input type="checkbox">.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified against the authoritative session log and the resulting file on disk.

observations.description: Before editing, the agent emitted a large pink/red injected 'rung 1' safety-ladder block and then a visible self-justification line ('Rung 1: no consequence beyond the lines touched ... Proceeding.'), which is noisy output for a one-line HTML edit.
The log shows TWO Edit tool calls on index.html for a single one-line change — the first apparently blocked/retried by the ladder hook ('retry this call now'). Possible wasted call/token cost.

No coding-agent-token-usage.json existed in the results directory at the time of my check (`ls` showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json), so I could not verify the headline token total the story references; presumably written at teardown.

Launcher required four manual confirmation dialogs (theme, security notes, trust folder, bypass permissions) before the prompt was available, despite the HOWTO claiming dialog-bypass state was seeded.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool calls: Bash(ls), Bash(git status...), Read index.html, Edit index.html (x2) — no clarifying questions asked; screen showed 'Added a checkbox to index.html:9' and 'Cogitated for 21s'. coding-agent-workdir/index.html contains '<input type="checkbox"> Done'.

jq over the session JSONL for tool_use entries named "Skill" returned no output: `jq -rc '...select(.type=="tool_use" and .name=="Skill")|.input'` printed nothing. The 4 'brainstorming' matches in the log are all from the injected system/skill-listing text (e.g. '- hyperpowers:brainstorming' in a skill_listing attachment), not an invocation.
